description: AstraTriage is an autonomous astronaut health monitoring and triage dashboard built for Moon-to-Mars missions with up to 20-minute communication delays. Powered by React and NASA Human Research Program thresholds, it tracks vitals, radiation, and behavioral metrics with color-coded alerts and interactive zero-G self-exam protocols. (Solo project)
summary: AstraTriage is an offline-first, deep-space medical triage dashboard built for astronauts on long-duration Mars and Artemis missions. Communication delays between Mars and Earth can reach up to 44 minutes round-trip, making real-time medical guidance from flight surgeons impossible during acute emergencies. AstraTriage bridges this critical autonomy gap by providing an on-board clinical decision support system grounded in NASA Human Research Program (HRP) thresholds and space health standards. The web application features real-time DSN light-lag tracking, interactive vital sign panels, zero-G anatomical self-exam checklists, Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) visual Amsler grid tests, and instant physiological scenario simulators (such as Solar Particle Events). When vital thresholds are breached, AstraTriage instantly flags critical risks and provides actionable countermeasures—such as directing crew members to shielded storm shelter modules. By combining deterministic local rule evaluation with structured DSN data packet exports, AstraTriage ensures crew survival and autonomous health management when communication blackouts sever Earth telemetry links entirely.
details:
• What it does & how it works: AstraTriage is a fully responsive web application that monitors, simulates, and evaluates astronaut health telemetry locally without requiring cloud connectivity or internet access. It tracks six primary HRP vital signs (Heart Rate, Blood Pressure, 30-Day Radiation Dosimetry, Circadian Sleep, Core Temperature, and Behavioral Index). Users can switch between mission profiles (Nominal Orbit, Solar Particle Alert, and Mars Transit Fatigue) or use live bio-sensor sliders to dynamically alter vitals. The app instantly cross-references these values against hardcoded NASA HRP/STD-3001 clinical limits. If a threshold is exceeded (e.g., radiation >50 mSv), the UI shifts to a critical red-alert state, displaying prioritized medical countermeasures. It also includes an interactive Zero-G anatomical body map for region-specific checklists and a built-in Amsler Grid tool for monocular SANS vision checks.
  • Benefits & Intended Impact: The primary impact is enabling total medical autonomy for astronauts facing deep-space communication blackouts and 22-minute one-way signal delays. It removes cognitive overload during high-stress emergencies by translating raw telemetry into clear, step-by-step triage actions.
  • Tools & Technologies Used: Developed using React, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, and deployed live on Vercel ([https://astratriage.vercel.app/](https://astratriage.vercel.app/)), with source code managed via GitHub ([https://github.com/HajaraAhmad/astratriage]and structured presentations built via Google Slides.
  • Creativity & Design Factors: AstraTriage moves beyond static pitch decks by delivering a fully interactive simulation dashboard. The interface was meticulously styled to mimic real aerospace command software, featuring high-contrast dark modes, dynamic alert banner correlation, and zero-latency local state evaluation.
dataRefs: NASA Human Research Program (HRP) & STD-3001 Standards
